what: routing.pinned and routing.pinned-fallback (default true) are applied as a candidate filter in the legacy pick paths, for requests of the pinned credential's provider only

With fallback on the pin applies only while the pinned credential can serve; with fallback off it always applies, so the request ends with the pinned credential's own error. An id that names no credential is ignored, since its provider is unknown and refusing would block both providers
evidence: routing_pin_test.go: pin serves only its provider (round-robin and most-room, with and without fallback), falls back on failure and while cooling, without fallback returns the pinned 429 and touches no other credential, unknown id ignored. Upstream's own tests define a headerless 429 as a genuine rate limit, and Claude-compatible gateways behind ClaudeExecutor can send one, so the rule is limited to this fork's honest modes, where Anthropic refusing the client is the known cause. The error type mirrors upstream's claudeEntitlementError
